issue: Discovery sweep (2026-06 europe, tracker-countries-only re-sweep) hunted for any Belgian LNG import/export terminal beyond the single GEM site (Zeebrugge LNG Terminal, Fluxys LNG, 5 unit-rows). Belgium is a mature single-terminal import market; LNG imports actually FELL ~29% in 2024 as German/Dutch FSRUs came online, so there is no demand-driven push for a second site. Every 2024-2026 signal resolves to existing GEM coverage or out-of-scope activity: (a) the 2024/2025 Zeebrugge regas expansions (+1.8 bcm/y in 2025; ~1.3 mtpa more sendout by early 2026; long-term nameplate rising 110->134 slots from Apr 2027) map to GEM's existing operating '2024 Expansion'/'2025 Expansion' units and Fluxys's Indicative Investment Plan 2024-2033, all at Zeebrugge; (b) the 'Zeebrugge Multi-molecule Hub' is GEM's existing proposed unit (G100002042603) and concerns low-carbon HYDROGEN/derivatives import + CO2 export, not LNG (none of the H2-derivative components have reached construction or FID per fluxys.com); (c) Port-of-Antwerp LNG activity (Fluxys/Titan LNG bunker pontoon, Cryostar/KC LNG fuelling facility, bio-LNG) is LNG BUNKERING/refuelling - excluded from tracker scope; (d) Belgian shipowner Exmar's FSRU-conversion charter is for the Eemshaven terminal in the NETHERLANDS (EemsEnergy Terminal / Gasunie-Vopak), not a Belgian terminal. No distinct second site, no FSRU chartered/deployed to Belgium, no FLNG/liquefaction export facility, and no in-scope (non-bunkering) new regas surfaced. IEEFA's European LNG Tracker and GEM.wiki are GEM-derived and were not treated as independent evidence (anti-circularity).
suggested_action: No action - no net-new Belgian LNG terminal or unit found beyond existing GEM coverage (Zeebrugge LNG Terminal: base + 2008/2024/2025 Expansions operating + proposed Multi-molecule Hub). Zeebrugge expansion specifics (capacity, slot counts, plan 2024-2033) belong to the Update workflow, not Discovery.
